title: Recursion & the call stack
hook: Recursion isn’t magic — it’s the same function calling itself, stacking frames, then unwinding.

steps.caption: fact(3) needs fact(2), so a new frame stacks on top.

nodeCaptions.f1: Waiting on the result of the inner call.
nodeCaptions.f2: Each call gets its own locals on the stack.

steps.caption: Keep stacking until you hit the base case.

nodeCaptions.base: Base case returns without calling again — otherwise you’d recurse forever.

steps.caption: Answers bubble back as frames pop: 1 → 2 → 6.

nodeCaptions.f1: Unwind is just returns. Deep recursion ⇒ deep stack.

takeaways: Recursion = call stack frames stacking, then returning.
Every recursive function needs a base case that stops the chain.
Too much depth overflows the stack — same memory region as normal calls.

quiz.question: What happens if a recursive function never hits a base case?
choices: Calls keep stacking until the stack overflows
The heap deletes older frames automatically
quiz.explanation: No base case means infinite (or until crash) recursion.
